incorporated as Bajaj Auto Finance Limited on 25 March 1987 as a non-banking financial company, the company primarily focused on providing two and three-wheeler finance.{{Cite web |last1=Sitaraman Ltd (Bajfinance) - Strategy, SWOT and Corporate Finance Report |url=https://store.marketline.com/report/mlfs27568fsa--bajaj-finance-ltd-bajfinance-strategy-swot-and-corporate-finance-report/ |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fUhkEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Bajaj+Finance%22&pg=PT401 |title=Rahul Bajaj: An Extraordinary Life |date=2022-03-21 |publisher=Penguin Random House India Private Limited |url=https://indiainfoline.com/company/bajaj-finance-ltd/summary/3722 |url-status=live |language=en}} In its first seven years, Bajaj Finance mainly borrowed wholesale and lent retail. |url-status=live }} ==Operations== As of March 2023, the company deals in consumer lending, SME (small and medium-sized enterprises) lending, commercial lending, rural lending, deposits, and wealth management.{{Cite web |title=Exploring the Next Generation Employee Experience: Case Study of Bajaj Finance Limited |url=https://www.thecasecentre.org/products/view?id=169800 |access-date=2022-03-17 |website=The Case Centre |language=en |archive-date=17 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220417134912/https://www.thecasecentre.org/products/view?id=169800 |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |last=John |first=Nevin |date=2023-10-10 |title=Bajaj Finance's Fire Fighter |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/long-reads/bajaj-finances-fire-fighter/114378 |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune India]] |language=en}} It has 294 consumer branches and 497 rural locations with over 33,000+ distribution points and 1,50,000+ stores.{{Cite web |date=7 July 2022 |first=Mayur |last=Shetty |title=Bajaj Fin's assets grow 31% to cross Rs 2L crore|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/bajaj-fins-assets-grow-31-to-cross-rs-2l-crore/articleshow/92709377.cms |access-date=2022-08-01 |website=The Times of India |language=en}} As of 30 September 2024, [[money market]]s made up 47% of company's borrowings, bank borrowings 29%, deposits 20%, and [[external commercial borrowing]]s 4%. It had deposits worth {{INRConvert|66131|c}}. Most of Bajaj Finance's revenue is generated from suppliers who pay for access to their customer base.{{Cite book |last=Bijapurkar |first=Rama |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OG7-EAAAQBAJ&dq=lilliput+land+bajaj+finance&pg=PT64 |title=Lilliput Land: How Small is Driving India's Mega Consumption Story |date=2024-02-29 |publisher=Penguin Random House India Private Limited |isbn=978-93-5708-379-9 |language=en}} As of December 2024, mortgages currently make up 31% of its consolidated AUM, while SME lending accounts for 14% and commercial lending for 13%. Bajaj Finance previously worked with [[RBL Bank]] and [[DBS Bank]] to issue co-branded credit cards.{{Cite web |last=Karthik |first=Hamsini |date=2022-08-18 |title=Bajaj Finance readies for entry into |archive-date=31 August 2022 |access-date=2022-08-31 |website=www.thehindubusinessline.com |language=en}} In early December 2024, the company ended its partnerships due to new [[Reserve Bank of Bajaj Finance Limited (BFL) is an Indian deposit-taking non-banking financial company (NBFC-UL) headquartered in Pune. It has 114.57 million customers and holds assets under management worth ₹509,975 crore (US$53 billion), as of April 2026.
As per the 2023 list of NBFCs issued by the Reserve Bank of India, Bajaj Finance is in the "upper layer" based on scale-based regulation guidelines.
